title: Aperiodic Thickness-Graded Stack for Broadened 8-13 μm Response
scientific_hypothesis: An aperiodic HfO2/SiO2 stack with chirped (graded) layer thicknesses will produce broader high-emissivity coverage across the full 8-13 μm atmospheric window compared to a periodic stack, while maintaining low emissivity in 3-5 μm.
design_principle: Varying layer thicknesses across the stack creates multiple overlapping resonances that broaden the high-emissivity band. Gradually changing optical thickness from front to back of the stack can create an impedance-matched transition that reduces reflection across a wider wavelength range.
proposed_topology: air | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | hfo2 | sio2 | si substrate, exactly 24 layers total (12 pairs)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers, initialized with linear chirp from 8000 nm to 13000 nm quarter-wave values
soft_objectives: maximize mean emissivity in 8000-13000 nm band
minimize mean emissivity in 3000-5000 nm band
maximize spectral uniformity (minimize variance) within 8000-13000 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: 24 layers uses the maximum allowed layer count
chirped thicknesses require precise deposition control
HfO2 and SiO2 are compatible with standard thin-film processes
theory_basis: Impedance matching through graded index structures
Multiple resonance superposition for bandwidth broadening
Literature L04 and L11 on dual-selective emitters
expected_advantages: Full 24-layer budget allows more degrees of freedom for optimization
Chirped design may achieve broader band coverage than periodic approach
Literature L04 supports dual-selective emitter concept
known_risks: More layers increase fabrication complexity and potential for defects
Aperiodic optimization may converge to local minima
L22 notes temperature-dependent effects not modeled here
execution_request_english: Design an aperiodic multilayer dielectric stack on silicon substrate with air incidence. Stack structure: air | (hfo2 | SiO2 (Kischkat))_12 | si, exactly 24 layers total. Optimize individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers, initialized with linear chirp from quarter-wave at 8000 nm (front) to quarter-wave at 13000 nm (back). Target: maximize mean emissivity in 8000-13000 nm band, minimize mean emissivity in 3000-5000 nm band, maximize spectral uniformity within 8000-13000 nm. Wavelength range for evaluation: 3000-13000 nm. Polarization: unpolarized (average TE and TM). Incidence angle: 0 degrees (normal). Material refractive indices from catalog datasets for hfo2, SiO2 (Kischkat), and si. Total layer count fixed at 24.
